items.text: Andoni Iraola used his pre-Ipswich press conference to back Cody Gakpo, saying the forward has trained well through pre-season and is now 'in a good place physically, mentally.' Ben C, who owns Gakpo, gets a settled attacking option as Liverpool try to open their away account tonight.

items.text: Iraola's press conference also covered the treatment room: Joe Gomez is closest to returning and should join training next week, Giovanni Leoni and Federico Chiesa are targeted for the international break, and Conor Bradley and especially Hugo Ekitike remain further away. None of those names sit in any of the six squads, but it is the backdrop as Ben C, Ben D, Marcus and Edward all lean on Liverpool players tonight.

source.title: Injury news: Iraola provides update on Gomez, Leoni, Chiesa, Bradley and Ekitike

items.text: Manchester City completed a British-record-equalling 125 million pound deadline-day deal for Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea, reuniting the World Cup winner with former boss Enzo Maresca. items.text: Cristhian Mosquera was withdrawn as a precaution in Arsenal's 1-0 win at Aston Villa after feeling discomfort, with Arteta saying afterwards 'he's fine, but he was feeling like he was about to have something.' items.text: Justin owns Erling Haaland and still sits last in the table, 41 points off Marcus at the top after two gameweeks. Having the most nailed-on forward in the game only helps if the other fourteen shirts turn up too.

Ben C has five of his fifteen players pencilled into Liverpool's likely XI at Ipswich tonight: Virgil, Frimpong, Szoboszlai, Gakpo and Isak. That is either the smartest stack in the league or the most stressful ninety minutes of his gameweek.

Alexander Isak scored twice in the opening ten minutes at Portman Road, both created by Cody Gakpo, as Liverpool beat Ipswich 2-0 for Andoni Iraola's first win in charge. Small Ben owns four of the Liverpool players who featured - Isak, Gakpo, Szoboszlai and Virgil van Dijk - and banked 33 points from them once the bonus settled - Isak 13, Gakpo 11, Van Dijk 6, Szoboszlai 3.

source.title: Alexander Isak scores twice to secure Liverpool win at Ipswich

items.text: Bradley Barcola made his first Liverpool appearance as a 64th-minute substitute in the win at Ipswich but did not add to the scoreline. Justin is the only one of the six to own him, and the cameo was worth exactly one point: a midfielder needs an hour on the pitch to take a share of the clean sheet, and Barcola got twenty-six minutes of it.

source.title: Alexander Isak scores twice to secure Liverpool win at Ipswich

items.text: Small Ben topped the live gameweek standings tonight on the back of four Liverpool players - Isak, Gakpo, Szoboszlai and Virgil - doing all the actual elevating. Fitting, since it is the closest Small Ben has ever come to being tall.

Marcus started the evening 27 points clear of Small Ben and finished it two ahead. One Liverpool match did that: Alisson's clean sheet, five saves and a bonus point were worth eight to Marcus, while Small Ben's four red shirts brought back thirty-three. Big Ben took three off Wirtz and Justin one for Barcola's cameo; Edward and Robert had nobody in the game and could only watch.

Alexander Isak thought he had a first-half hat-trick at Portman Road when a Florian Wirtz pass sent him through again, but the goal was ruled out for offside and he had to settle for the two that stood. Isak said afterwards it capped a mentally tough spell: 'It was a long injury, a difficult season in general... that season is kind of behind me now, but it wasn't easy.' Ben C still banked both goals that counted, and Big Ben's Wirtz picked up the assist on the one that did not.

source.title: Ipswich 0-2 Liverpool: Andoni Iraola up and running as Reds boss with Alexander Isak at the double

items.text: Robert's gap to the top went from 22 points to 30 on Friday night without a single one of his players setting foot on a pitch: he had nobody in the only game on. Pardinho's title odds are receding just like his hairline, and both managed it while he sat there doing nothing at all.

Mikel Arteta said Jurrien Timber is back in full training and 'in a really good place' as he nears a return from the groin injury that has kept him out for months. Arteta also confirmed Cristhian Mosquera, substituted as a precaution against Aston Villa, remains available for Sunday's game with Chelsea, easing any worry for Robert, who owns him.

Big Ben's only man in it, B.Fernandes, played the full ninety and returned two points while Mbeumo scored, Mainoo set one up and Shaw set another - the most expensive shirt on the pitch, and the least involved in the goals.

Morgan Rogers put Chelsea ahead inside two minutes at the Emirates, Kai Havertz leveled in the 25th, and Martin Odegaard put Arsenal 2-1 up in the 50th, where it finished. Rogers and Havertz are both Big Ben's; Odegaard is Edward's.

items.text: Marcus went into the gameweek 27 clear of Ben C, 120 to 93. Ben C outscored him 60 to 44 across it, sixteen points of the gap gone in three days, and is still 11 short: Marcus 164, Ben C 153 once the game adds it up. FPL has not closed the gameweek yet, so its own table will keep saying 150 to 146 with Ben C on top until it does - that is the standings lagging, not the lead.
Marcus's waiver business gets called kneejerk central round here, and Elanga is exhibit A. Whatever the case for picking him up, today's return was 1 point - hardly a rebuttal.

Big Ben leans on Bruno to bail him out, or so the theory goes, and when Bruno doesn't haul the team is awful. Today Bruno managed 2 points and Big Ben finished the day fifth of six - the theory holds up fine.

Big Ben gets branded a biased Gunners fan more than anyone else in this league, and today's book-keeping backs it up: three Arsenal shirts in his fifteen - White, Havertz and Konsa - combined for 14 of his 27 points, more than half the day's work. There are worse things to be than biased when the fixtures fall your way like that.

Mikel Arteta said after Sunday's 2-1 win over Chelsea that Kai Havertz "looks happy, looks settled" and is contributing goals as well as defensive work, and praised Ezri Konsa's full debut against Joao Pedro despite the defender having had only five or six training sessions since his move. Big Ben owns both Havertz and Konsa.

items.text: Six managers, a full waiver wire between them, and the week's individual podium still belonged to nobody's team: Mitchell (15), Bogle (14), Barnes (12) and Vuskovic (12) are all free agents, and the best any rostered player did was Small Ben's Isak on 13. A league this obsessed with each other's squads left the actual scouting to whoever did not claim them.

Justin still has Erling Haaland, who put in 9 today, and it did not stop two different managers going past him on the same day: Edward into third on 133 and Big Ben into fourth on 129, leaving Schwaddy fifth on 124. Some squads are just not built to be carried by one man.

Robert's total after three gameweeks is 120. Marcus had already banked that much before a ball was kicked in the third one. A whole season as somebody else's warm-up act is not a flattering stat, and Pardinho now has a week off to sit with it.

Newcastle and Bournemouth shared a 2-2 draw at St James' Park on Saturday. Marcus Tavernier's early strike and a Malick Thiaw own goal put the visitors 2-0 up before Harvey Barnes and an 88th-minute Jacob Ramsey goal rescued a point for Newcastle. Justin owns the scoring Tavernier; Ben D's Thiaw was the man who put the ball in his own net.
